text_blocks.snippet: Mount Everest is the highest mountain in the world above sea level, while Mauna Kea is the tallest mountain from base to peak.
Different Ways to Measure a Mountain

list.snippet: Highest Above Sea Level: Mount Everest reaches 29,031.69 feet (8,848.86 meters) above sea level, making it the highest altitude on Earth.
Tallest from Base to Peak: Mauna Kea in Hawaii rises over 33,500 feet (10,210 meters) from the ocean floor to its summit, though only 13,802 feet (4,207 meters) are above water.
Furthest from Earth's Center: Mount Chimborazo in Ecuador bulges outward because the Earth is wider at the equator, placing its peak farthest from the center of the planet.
